parsed.rationale: The cluster surfaces `HSBColor.uiColor` (line 53) and `HSBColor.nsColor` (line 63) in `Shared/ColorPalette/Sources/ColorPalette/HSBColor.swift` as near-duplicates with a Jaccard similarity of 0.71, meaning roughly 71 % of their token structure is shared. Both are computed properties on the same type in the same file and in the same `ColorPalette` package, differing only in the platform color type they construct. Extracting the shared HSB-component assembly into a private helper would eliminate the duplication while preserving the distinct platform-typed public surface. No context flags (test, codegen, mock, sample-app) suggest the duplication is intentional.

specifics.proposed_action: Introduce a private helper method on `HSBColor` (e.g., `func makeColor(usingUIKit: Bool) -> AnyObject` or, more idiomatically, a shared `func colorComponents() -> (hue: CGFloat, saturation: CGFloat, brightness: CGFloat, alpha: CGFloat)`) that encapsulates the common HSB-to-platform-color conversion logic. Both `uiColor` and `nsColor` then delegate to this helper, keeping their platform-specific return types (`UIColor` / `NSColor`) while eliminating the duplicated body. Alternatively, if the project targets both iOS and macOS, consider a `#if canImport(UIKit)` / `#if canImport(AppKit)` conditional compilation block with a single `color` computed property that resolves to the correct type, removing the need for two separate properties entirely.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: The two properties (`HSBColor.uiColor` at line 53 and `HSBColor.nsColor` at line 63) are near-duplicates (Jaccard 0.71) that exist to serve two different platform APIs (`UIColor` on iOS/tvOS, `NSColor` on macOS). They are not candidates for generic-parameterization (the return types are platform-specific nominal types, not a single generic parameter), not for protocol-inheritance or default-implementation (there is no protocol involved), and not for subclass-lift (HSBColor is not a class hierarchy). The most idiomatic Swift remedy is either a shared private helper or a conditional-compilation alias — neither of which maps cleanly to any of the named refactor categories.
